summary: 5-second connectTimeout blocks server startup when Redis is unavailable
failure_scenario: When Redis is down at startup, the rate-limiter's dedicated IORedis client blocks for 5 full seconds on the initial connectTimeout before failing. Since createRedisRateLimitStore() is called during server boot (server.js), this delays the entire application becoming ready. With maxRetriesPerRequest: null and enableOfflineQueue: false, every subsequent request fails immediately, triggering 6 string.includes() checks per request even though Redis errors are rare.

summary: maxSsePerIp computed on every SSE connection from a static config value
failure_scenario: Math.max(10, Math.floor(config.maxSseClients / 50)) executes on every new SSE connection (potentially hundreds over the server's lifetime). config.maxSseClients is an env var that never changes at runtime, so the result is always the same constant. Should be hoisted to module scope as a constant rather than recomputed per-connection.

summary: Two full-DOM querySelector calls per tab switch instead of cached references
failure_scenario: document.querySelector('.nav-btn.active') and document.querySelector('.tab-content.active') each traverse the entire DOM tree on every tab switch. With 20+ elements, this adds ~0.1ms per switch. Since the previous active elements are known from the prior tab state, these could be tracked as component state (this.prevActiveBtn / this.prevActiveContent) instead of re-querying the DOM.
